chunks: ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar, meaning the second, peace be upon him, about a man who appointed me as his executor and instructed me to give something to his uncle every year, then the uncle died.
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "Give it to his heirs."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed by bequest or entrusted through a will
key_terms.أُعْطِيَ: to give or deliver the assigned payment
key_terms.عَمًّا: a paternal uncle, the designated beneficiary here
key_terms.كُلِّ سَنَةٍ: every year, indicating a recurring payment
key_terms.وَرَثَتَهُ: his heirs, who receive the entitlement after his death

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shia fiqh if the beneficiary of a bequest dies before receiving the bequeathed payment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a recurring bequest assigned to a specified relative. If the designated recipient dies, what was to be given to him is instead given to his heirs, indicating continuity of the financial entitlement through inheritance.
